thread:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: ALERT: cont-batch-p99 latency spike in us-west1, 5xx rate > 0.5% for 5m. page: @oncall
maya: grabbing dashboards... queue depth is climbing, s->processing queue meters at 1200, microbatch_size showing bursts to 256+ for several hosts
aj: oncall here. seeing sudden rise in prefetch evictions and kvcache miss ratio -> memory thrash. correlates with high concurrent sessions from customer 'Parkly'
maya: Parkly reported orders timing out. PD ticket 3456 opened. can we throttle concurrency for that tenant?
aj: can try routing that tenant to lower concurrency pool and cap per-connection microbatch to 64 temporarily
sre-bot: stack traces from host rtx-12-7:
```
runtime: continuous_batch.cpp:evict_cache(): kv_evictions++
runtime: batch_coalesce.cpp:emit(): microbatch_size=256 -> enqueue latency 300ms
```
dmitri: logs show repeated KV regen and large prefetch loops causing backlog. suspect prefetch heuristic bug combined with new model seq len.
maya: tentative mitigation plan: 1) disable prefetch on affected pool 2) apply microbatch cap 3) restart a subset of worker processes to clear KV cache 4) monitor
emily: +1. how fast can we push those config changes? we need minimal customer impact
aj: I can do the config patch to feature flag 'microbatch_max_tokens=64' and 'prefetch.enabled=false' for pool 'usw1-highcpu' now. will push as hotfix (no compile) via runtime-config API
maya: if we restart workers, KV cache will be lost — good for clearing blowup but increases cold-start latency. weigh tradeoffs
aj: doing hotfix now. command:
```
curl -X POST https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/runtime-config \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
 -d '{"pool":"usw1-highcpu","microbatch_max_tokens":64,"prefetch_enabled":false}'
```
opsbot: deploy started by aj — hotfix config rollout to 12 hosts
sre-bot: telemetry: 3 hosts failed to apply config (OOM on agent), they're being drained
maya: starting phased restart of 6 worker procs on drained hosts
pagerbot: Incident created: INC-2026-1123. Severity: high. Paging on-call escalation in 5m
aj: initial effects: p99 down from 2.8s -> 1.1s on patched hosts; overall 5xx rate dropped to 0.12%
dmitri: monitoring KV eviction rate — dropping after restarts and prefetch toggle
emily: customer update draft: "We saw elevated latency & timeouts due to an internal batching regression. We've applied mitigations and are restoring normal performance. We'll follow up with root cause." any objections?
maya: fine. add that we're performing full RCA and will share timeline
aj: rolling back feature flag isn't needed; hotfix seems stable. recommend keeping prefetch off for 4 hours then re-enable with lower aggressiveness
dmitri: capturing logs for RCA: correlating model version 2026-03-07 and seq-len distribution spike at 01:42 UTC
maya: handing off to emily for night-watch at 23:00 UTC — include mitigation steps, current status, and customer comms. all relevant links:
- dashboards: https://grafana.internal/d/cont-batch-usw1
- runbook excerpt: "kb/continuous-batching/eviction-mitigation"
emily: ack taking over. will monitor latency and 5xx for next 3 hours, escalate if p99 > 1.5s or 5xx > 0.5%
maya: leaving note: no rollback required, hotfix applied, partial restarts completed, customer Parkly notified via PD ticket 3456. handoff complete :white_check_mark:
emily: saw a small re-burst at +18m but not sustained. keeping prefetch off until morning. :thumbsup:
